name: Reverse-current measuring relay
summary: Measuring relay that operates when current flows in the opposite direction to normal, such as back-feed into a DC source.
description: A reverse-current relay compares the direction of current with a reference and operates when current flows the wrong way. Classic uses are DC generators and battery chargers in parallel, where a failed source would otherwise draw current from the bus, and rectifier feeders where back-feed indicates a fault.

On the schematic the relay box carries a current quantity with a direction qualifier, and its contacts are drawn elsewhere in the trip or alarm circuit. The box does not show the pick-up level or time delay, and in AC systems the equivalent requirement is usually met with a directional power function rather than a simple current-direction element.
readingNotes: Identify which direction is treated as normal for the source.
Find the contacts that trip or disconnect the source.
distinction: A reverse-current relay responds to current direction; a maximum-current relay responds to magnitude regardless of direction.
